Some of history's biggest ideas came from dreams

Mendeleev dreamed the periodic table. McCartney dreamed "Yesterday."

Neither of them remembered by accident. Most people forget the same kind of moment before they even reach for their phone.

The periodic table

Chemist Dmitri Mendeleev spent days trying to organize the elements. He fell asleep at his desk, and by his own account, saw the entire table in a dream, then woke up and wrote it down almost exactly as it appears today.

"Yesterday"

Paul McCartney woke up with the entire melody already in his head. He was so sure he'd heard it somewhere before, he spent weeks checking he hadn't accidentally stolen it.
